title: leafblower benchmark study — problem spec
description: Design of record: docs/benchmark/DESIGN.md §3. One JSON file per problem (canonical home-turf, stepstone, synthetic-family). Bulk data is referenced via a typed data_ref, never inlined; only scalars/small arrays are inline. Loaded by common/problem_io.{R,py} into a standardized problem object (see loader docstrings for the exact field list).

id.description: Unique problem id; also used as the runs.parquet `problem` key and as the weights/<solver>__<problem>__... filename component (§8).

data_ref.description: Typed origin. 'file:<path.parquet|.csv>' — bulk data on disk, path relative to repo root (never inlined). 'pkg:<package>::<dataset>' — package-bundled canonical dataset, resolved via that language's own package API each arm (single-arm by nature: an R-only package has no Python resolution, and vice versa — NOT a bug). 'gen:<recipe_id>' — parametric synthetic-family generator (WU-3 scope; the schema/dispatch point is defined here, the recipes are not — resolving one raises a clear not-yet-implemented error). 'inline' — small toy arrays, embedded in the `data` field of this same spec.

data.description: Inline rows (array of flat objects, one per observation). Required iff data_ref == 'inline'; absent for all other origins (bulk data must never be inlined — Constraint III/Format).

design_weights.description: Per-observation design weights d_i (harvest()'s `design_weights=` arg — there is NO `weights=` arg, CLAUDE.md). One of: omitted/null (defaults to all-ones, i.e. self-weighting sample); 'column:<name>' (read from a column of the resolved data, e.g. a package's own `pw`); or an inline JSON array of length n (only meaningful for data_ref=='inline').

margins.description: Column names in the resolved data that carry the K calibration margins. Must have exactly K entries and must equal the key set of the resolved targets.

targets_ref.description: Path (relative to repo root) to a JSON file of {margin: {category: count_or_proportion}} (e.g. benchmarks/stepstone_fulldata_bench_targets.json). Mutually exclusive with `targets`; the loader normalizes each margin's values to proportions summing to 1 (raw counts are accepted, matching the existing stepstone target file convention).

targets.description: Inline {margin: {category: count_or_proportion}}, for small/toy problems. Mutually exclusive with `targets_ref`.

bounds.description: Weight box bounds, passed to harvest()'s min_weight/max_weight. null means unbounded on that side: min -> 0 (weights are non-negative by convention), max -> +Inf (harvest.R:454 explicitly allows +Inf as 'unbounded').

tol.description: Shared convergence tolerance; mapped to each solver's native stopping parameter by the (separately committed) tol-mapping table (DESIGN.md §5) — this spec only carries the shared nominal value.

objective_families.description: Objective families this problem is applicable to, for registry.json cross-checking (DESIGN.md §3).

K.description: Margin count; must equal length(margins). Kept as an explicit redundant field (not just derived) so registry.json / solver applicability checks (K_max) don't need to load+resolve the full problem just to know K.
